title: Book pickups through a Calendar-based dispatch library

blocks.text: The courier service books pickups through a dispatch library written before Java 8. It takes the requested pickup as a `GregorianCalendar`, and returns the confirmed pickup as a `Calendar` in the depot's zone. Each depot is configured with a zone ID. Last month a depot was configured with a misspelled ID and its pickups were booked hours off for two weeks before anyone noticed, and the drivers' app sometimes shows a confirmed pickup at a time that is right on no clock at the depot.
`DispatchAdapter.book(...)` already calls the library. Finish the three `TODO` methods in `src/main/java/practice/DispatchAdapter.java`:

items: `depotZone(configuredId)`: the depot's zone for the library, refusing an ID that names no zone;
`toLibrary(pickup)`: the calendar to hand the library;
`fromLibrary(returned)`: the confirmed pickup, as the moment the calendar holds in its own zone.

blocks.text: The servers' default zone must make no difference; the tests use depots in several zones and never change it. About three lines in total.

cases.says: a pickup booked through the library comes back as the same moment
a depot configured with a valid zone ID gets that zone
a depot configured with a misspelled zone ID is refused with a DateTimeException
the calendar handed to the library has the pickup's zone and hour, for depots in two zones
a calendar the library returns is read in that calendar's zone, for depots in two zones
a calendar that is not a GregorianCalendar converts too

origin.section: A Calendar Converts With Its Own Zone, Not the JVM's

concepts: GregorianCalendar.from and toZonedDateTime keep the calendar's zone; toInstant drops it, so the zone attached next must be the calendar's own, not the JVM's default.
Only GregorianCalendar has toZonedDateTime; any other Calendar converts with toInstant and getTimeZone().toZoneId().
TimeZone.getTimeZone(String) turns an unknown ID into GMT, while TimeZone.getTimeZone(ZoneId.of(id)) rejects it.
